summary: TWO-WEEK WINDOW (Aug 28 - Sept 11), reported as one period because the Sept 4 run crashed before delivery. 60 messages, 30 from her, 30 from ALTR. The window contains the single most dangerous message this client has ever sent and the single worst piece of follow-through on the account. On Aug 30 Mayson re-sent the same content Drive link Michelle first sent on 2026-05-07 and imposed a quota — '7 reels a week so 30 in total per month', fresh content only. She replied in two minutes asking the question she has now asked in five separate months: 'how are the instagrams doing that you guys post on? as I haven’t heard much, can you please send me the links to them?' She got two links and 'Working on it!!'. Three days later she supplied the numbers herself — 'compare your accounts which is getting roughly 150 views per post which just isn’t profitable compare to me posting it myself' — refused the quota on economic grounds, and 33 minutes after that wrote a calm, structured verdict on the Instagram service: the editing and management are 'quite poor', the same songs keep repeating, and her friend's management grew two extra accounts to 'around 40k followers' on the identical brief by re-editing existing content. She then asked ALTR to put a named specialist on her accounts. Fifth escalation of the same growth complaint (May 20, Jun 2, Jun 4, Jul 21, Sept 2) and the first time she has measured us, benchmarked a rival agency and asked for the staff to be replaced. It sat 28 hours until she typed '@mmayson ?'; Mayson replied in 15 minutes and booked a call for Sept 4 at 10:30am UK — the first call on this account since Jul 26. THEN NOTHING. Sept 4 contains zero messages. In the seven days since, no one has written a word to her about the editing, the staffing request, the quota she refused, or the accounts. Her biggest message of the quarter is 9 days old and has never received a substantive answer. On Sept 10 Michelle re-sent the identical Drive link as if the Sept 2 messages had not happened. Derrek sent ZERO messages across the entire fourteen days: 21 days since his last message of any kind (a two-word '@olkmck' on Aug 21), 41 days since anything substantive, and his Aug 2 Meta-rep money question is now 40 days unanswered. The $40k phone-farm 'plenty of updates starting next week' is 41 days old with one uncaptioned screenshot as the whole output. Wesley's anniversary sends are 31 and 28 days past with still zero trace anywhere — fourth consecutive report. The block list is 124 days. Against all that, three things genuinely went right in the back half. Vivek was excellent: she flagged a fresh Instagram restriction with screenshots on Sept 6, Mayson tagged him within 49 minutes, and he had it 'Fixed' by Sept 7 — closing the restriction thread that had been open since Jul 21. Ollie broke 19 days of silence on Sept 8 to chase the three customs she had forgotten; she apologised, asked to be chased harder next time, and uploaded all three on Sept 10. And the Aug 15-31 invoice was paid — but slowly, at 6 days, her slowest cycle in nine, after her UK bank blocked the transfer on Sept 5.
